questions.q: Which of these failures should get automatic retries with increasing waits between attempts?
options: An AI output that is missing a required field
A response whose stop reason is "refusal"
A timeout or rate limit from a busy service
An incoming message with only an attachment
questions.explain: Only temporary errors, such as timeouts, rate limits and busy services, deserve automatic retries with backoff. Retrying a bad input or a refusal on autopilot just fails again.

questions.q: Your CRM step timed out and was retried automatically, and now some leads appear twice in your CRM. What is the best fix?
options: Give each run a unique key, check it before acting and use find-or-create
Turn off retries entirely so that every step only ever runs once
Increase the wait between retries to give the CRM more time to respond
Have a reviewer delete the duplicate records from the CRM each week
questions.explain: An idempotency check prevents duplicates: a unique key per run, a check against the run log before any action, find-or-create instead of create, and recording the key once the action succeeds.

questions.q: The AI step in your lead workflow is failing, and a new enquiry arrives through your form. Which fallback does the lesson recommend?
options: Leave the submission unprocessed until someone notices the error
Retry the AI step every minute until it responds again
Discard the submission and ask the lead to try again later
Save the lead tagged "unclassified" and send your standard acknowledgment
questions.explain: A non-AI fallback keeps things moving: the lead is still saved to the CRM tagged "unclassified" and gets your standard acknowledgment, so the customer never notices.
